subject: SentryAI renewal: reliability incident follow-up & proposed expansion path
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentryai.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — latency spikes & availability concerns

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking time to read this. Over the last 6 weeks we've seen two production windows where tail latency for our event-processing jobs spiked above 2.5s per request for ~18 minutes. The incidents caused retries in our downstream pipelines and triggered a partial degradation in our UI.

We're preparing to renew our contract in October but wanted to raise this as a blocker — the team is asking for a formal path to higher availability (a stronger SLA and dedicated capacity options) before we sign an expansion.

Could you share what mitigation/remediation options Redwood can offer? Specifically:
- A path to a >=99.9% uptime commitment for our core inference endpoints
- A migration/upgrade plan to a dedicated pool for our high-throughput jobs
- Any credits or remediation you typically offer after repeat incidents

Copying procurement (procurement@sentryai.com) who will own the contractual side. Happy to jump on a short call this week.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, SentryAI

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentryai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency spikes & availability concerns

Alex — thanks for the clear note and for looping procurement. Sorry to hear about the disruption. We take these events seriously and I want to ensure you and your team have a concrete, time-bound path to stability before renewal.

Short answer: yes — we can propose a dedicated-pool pilot, an uplifted SLA, and a remediation credit framework. I'd like Ben (SE) to share a quick technical mitigation analysis and Irene (CS) to propose a pilot runbook and MOP (method of procedure).

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to provide an initial technical write-up and estimated cost delta (today, EOD).
2) Internal review + proposed pilot plan (Irene) by Friday.
3) 30-minute exec review with you + procurement next week to align on contract changes.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min meeting on Thu 9/10 or Mon 9/14? Also, could you attach the incident logs (request ids, approximate timestamps) if you have them?

Thanks — talk soon.

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentryai.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency spikes & availability concerns

Alex — quick technical note based on the sample traces you pasted in the incident summary. High-level findings:
- Pattern: tail latency correlated with concurrent long-context streaming workloads plus a burst of small inference requests.
- Root cause candidate: suboptimal batching + KV cache pressure on shared-hosted pools during peak concurrency.

Mitigations we can enact quickly:
1) Dedicated pool for your core endpoints (isolates KV cache, ensures no noisy-neighbor batching interference).
2) Prefix caching for frequent short prompts (low-effort config change; immediate latency wins).
3) Aggressive continuous-batching policy with size/latency knobs tuned to your request-size distribution.

Estimated impact: moving to a 2-node dedicated pool with conservative autoscaling should reduce tail by ~60–75% in our experience. Cost delta: roughly 28% over current hosted spend (rough estimate — I'll provide a line-item by EOD).

Attachment: sentry-diagnostic-summary.txt (attached) — short telemetry excerpt and suggested config template.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentryai.com>

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — latency spikes & availability concerns

Thanks Ben — that write-up is helpful. Procurement here — quick clarifying Qs before the exec sync:
- If SentryAI moves to a dedicated pool, what can Redwood commit to in writing for uptime (SLO vs SLA)?
- In the event we see another repeat incident within the next 90 days, what credits or remedies do you offer?
- Can you provide an estimated timeline for a migration pilot (including smoke tests and rollback plan)?

From our side: we're willing to sign a 12–18 month increase in committed spend if we get stronger uptime guarantees and operational runbooks.

—Carly (Procurement)
procurement@sentryai.com

From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sentryai.com>, Procurement <procurement@sentryai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed mutual action plan & commercial path for a dedicated pilot

Carly / Alex — thanks. Below is a concise mutual action plan (MAP) and commercial outline we can turn into a contract amendment: 

1) Pilot scope (2 weeks canary + 4 weeks full pilot): dedicated 2-node pool with conservative autoscale for your three production endpoints.
2) Uptime commitment: Redwood will provide a 99.9% availability SLA for endpoints on the dedicated pool during the pilot and for the negotiated term (we will define measurement windows and excluded maintenance in the amendment).
3) Remedy: In the unlikely event of availability <99.9% in a monthly measurement window, Redwood will provide pro-rated service credits. For repeat incidents (two distinct monthly windows within 90 days) we will escalate to: a) an additional one-time service credit equal to 10% of monthly committed spend, and b) a joint incident review with engineering and remediation plan.
4) Timeline: pilot can begin within 10 business days of signature (we'll need a brief infra onboarding call and an SSO/KMS checklist).
5) Price delta: estimated +28% committed monthly spend vs current hosted usage; line-item pricing and draft amendment attached.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pilot-outline.pdf, sentry-sla-comparison.xlsx

Next step: I propose a 30-min contract + engineering alignment on Mon 9/14 at 10:00am PT. If that works, we'll kick off the formal amendment and procurement review.

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Rachel — thanks for the MAP and the attachments. We have internal approval to proceed with the pilot under the terms outlined, pending a short amendment to the Master Services Agreement that captures: 1) the 99.9% pilot SLA, 2) the credit ladder for repeat incidents, and 3) an explicit 10-business-day start after countersignature.

Please send a redline of the amendment or a DocuSign link and we'll return an executed copy quickly. Target: start pilot week of 10/5.
